cs.t: If I needed to build up a wireless home network again, I'd just use old computers and Ubuntu.  https://help.ubuntu.com/stable/ubuntu-help/net-wireless-adho...  Or raspberry pi's  https://www.raspberrypi.org/documentation/configuration/wire...  Setting up your own network sounds way more technically involved than buying a box off the shelf access points. It's a little more technically demanding but I found it rewarding and stable over the long term. I had two Buffalo airstations and an old WRT-54G all running continuously for several years until the WRT-54G was retired. The hardest part was overcoming the my mental model that routers are one thing and computers are another and that wireless networks require something that says "router" on the box. But an iPhone can serve as a hotspot. So that's an option too. Finally, a good solution for bandwidth issues on a wireless network is to use CAT cable instead of radio wherever possible...when wireless is a problematic technology, use something else.
cs.th: Ask HN: What home networking equipment are you using?

cs.t: It's older now, but for several years I used a Buffalo N300 router which came pre-flashed running DDRWT out of the box:  https://www.buffalotech.com/products/airstation-highpower-n3...  I say "used" because my main router has been updated to an AC1900 solution, but it's still kicking, I'm just running it as an access point. Unfortunately, both it and their updated AC1200 solution:  https://www.buffalotech.com/products/airstation-ac1200-gigab...  are discontinued. Also, while it's pre-flashed with open-source software, it's not Open Source Hardware.
